name: Old Church Slavonic
confidence_why: Nandris 1959, Vondrák 1912, Leskien 1919 and Polivanova 2023, with De Bray 1969 and Schenker 1995 concurring, all state that the Old Church Slavonic manuscripts do not mark stress (only the Kiev Folia carry inconsistent diacritics) and that the accent can be reconstructed only by comparison with the modern Slavic languages, so no source disputes the undetermined record.
catalog_citation: Nandris, Grigore. 1959 (repr. with corrections 1965, repr. 1969). Handbook of Old Church Slavonic, Part I: Old Church Slavonic Grammar. London: The Athlone Press (University of London), section 4 'Quantity, Stress, and Intonation', pp. 9-10 [archive.org text …
catalog_locator: Nandris 1959 Part I, section 4 'Quantity, Stress, and Intonation', pp. 9-10 (text-layer, running head 'IO QUANTITY, STRESS, AND INTONATION §4' …
catalog_quote: Nandris 1959 section 4 (pp. 9-10): "The OCS texts, with the exception of the Kiev Miss., do not mark the quantity or the stress. The Kiev Miss, frequently uses diacritic signs over vowels ... these signs were probably intended to indicate the quantity or the stress, though they are used inconsistently. ... There is, however, no direct evidence concerning quantity, stress, and intonation in the historical period of OCS. It is, moreover, only by a comparative study of stress and intonation (or quantity) in the modern Slavonic languages, especially in Russian and Serbo-Croat, that one can conclude that CS had a free (movable) expiratory stress and a musical intonation (pitch). This could be either acute (rising ') or circumflex (rising-falling ~). ... In CS, these three phonemic elements (quantity, stress, intonation) were independent of each other, i.e. an unstressed vowel could be long, …

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding Nandris 1959 sec. 4 quotation is verbatim in the held archive.org text at the stated section and running head (pp. 9-10); the De Bray supporting quote is verbatim too (page is 3, not 4 -- cosmetic). (2) Deciding source is a 1959 reference grammar (Glottolog 'grammar', 235 pp) with a dedicated stress section; for a dead manuscript language the only possible finding is 'stress not recorded in the texts; Common Slavic free mobile stress with pitch reconstructed comparatively', and every other grammar opened now says the same: Vondrak 1912 p. 75 ('Über den Akzent im Aksl. wissen wir nichts Sicheres, da er.. nicht bezeichnet wurde'), Leskien 1919 sec. 5 (quantity 'nicht überliefert'), Schenker 1995 sec. 3.18 and n. 333 (held), and the newest open-access grammar, Polivanova 2023 p. 411 n. 25 (accentual properties 'remain unobservable or unknown for OCS').

sources.citation: Schaeken, Jos. 2008. Nochmals zur Akzentuierung der Kiever Blätter. In: A. Lubotsky, J. Schaeken & J. sources.note: Study of the Kiev Folia's diacritics: acute = accent place, grave = unaccented final syllable, open bow = vowel length; 'Tonzeichen' means accent signs, no pitch contrast is discussed.

tone.quote: Dabei beschränke ich mich auf die Deutung der drei Tonzeichen (Gravis/вария, Akut/оксия und Zirkumflex/периспомена) sowie des Dauerzeichens (кремаста) ... In den von Zagrebin behandelten serbischen Handschriften können alle vier diakritischen Zeichen Vokallänge andeuten, während dies in den Kiever Blättern nur für den nach oben offenen Bogen gilt. • Das einzige Zeichen der Betonung ist in den Kiever Blättern der Akut. ... In den Kiever Blättern ist der Gravis dagegen gerade das Zeichen der Tonlosigkeit einer Endsilbe.
tone.locator: p. 492, end of sec. 2 exposition and p. 494 bullets 1-2
tone.translation: Here I confine myself to the interpretation of the three tone signs (grave/varija, acute/oksija and circumflex/perispomena) and of the length sign (kremasta) ... In the Serbian manuscripts treated by Zagrebin all four diacritics can indicate vowel length, whereas in the Kiev Folia this holds only for the upward-open bow. • The only sign of stress in the Kiev Folia is the acute. ... In the Kiev Folia the grave, by contrast, is precisely the sign of the unaccentedness of a final syllable.
tone.summary: Study of the Kiev Folia's diacritics: acute = accent place, grave = unaccented final syllable, open bow = vowel length; 'Tonzeichen' means accent signs, no pitch contrast is discussed.
tone.says: Study of the Kiev Folia's diacritics: acute = accent place, grave = unaccented final syllable, open bow = vowel length; 'Tonzeichen' means accent signs, no pitch contrast is discussed.

sources.citation: Schaeken, Jos. 1988. Zur Funktion der supralinearen Zeichen in den Kiever Blättern. In: Klaus Trost, Ekkehard Völkl & Erwin Wedel (eds.), Symposium Methodianum: Beiträge der internationalen Tagung in Regensburg (17. bis 24. April 1985) zum Gedenken an den 1100. Todestag des hl. Method (Selecta Slavica 13), 663-668. Neuried: Hieronymus. [host volume: ISBN 3-88893-075-8, OCLC 19877984, XIII+727 pp.]
sources.note: Schaeken divides the Kiev Folia's diacritics into (a) spiritus signs (asper/lenis over the initial vowel of almost 92% of words; the lenis marks a possible prejotation of a, e, eN) and (b) four further signs, three shaped like the Greek accents (gravis, acute, circumflex) plus an upward-open bow, read either as accents or as neumes. He sets Koschmieder's neume theory aside as untenable (quoting Kortlandt 1980: 1 n.1) and builds on Trubetzkoy's (1954: 43-50) functional analysis: the gravis marks the tonelessness ('Tonlosigkeit') of a final syllable, 34x over monosyllabic pro-/enclitics and 5x…

tone.quote: Mislim da nemamo prava smatrati napore najvećih autoriteta na području slavenske lingvistike — Karinskog, Grunskog, Vondraka, Kuljbakina, Jagića, Weingarta, Trubeckog — za besplodnu igru s rješavanjem lingvističkih rebusa, već da moramo u znakovima Kijevskih listića gledati sistem prozodijskih znakova preuzet iz Vizantije, ali stvaralački prilagođen prikazivanju posebnih svojstava slavenskog izgovora. ... potreba da se za celebranta sačuvaju oznake kako treba izgovarati tekst s obzirom na naglasak i kvantitet slogova.
tone.locator: p. 45, concluding discussion before the asterisk break
tone.translation: I think we have no right to regard the efforts of the greatest authorities in Slavic linguistics — Karinskij, Grunskij, Vondrák, Kul'bakin, Jagić, Weingart, Trubetzkoy — as a fruitless game of solving linguistic puzzles, but that we must see in the signs of the Kiev Folia a system of prosodic signs taken over from Byzantium, yet creatively adapted to represent the particular properties of Slavic pronunciation. ... the need to preserve for the celebrant indications of how the text is to be pronounced with regard to the accent and the quantity of syllables.
tone.summary: Philological study of Kiev Folia diacritics: acute = word-accent place, upturned arc = vowel length, grave/circumflex follow Greek spelling; no claim about distinctive pitch. Accent-marked forms only.
tone.says: Philological study of Kiev Folia diacritics: acute = word-accent place, upturned arc = vowel length, grave/circumflex follow Greek spelling; no claim about distinctive pitch. Accent-marked forms only.

sources.citation: Koschmieder, Erwin. 1955. Die vermeintlichen Akzentzeichen der Kiever Blätter. Slovo: časopis Staroslavenskoga instituta u Zagrebu 4-5: 5-23.
sources.note: Denies that the Kiev Folia diacritics record OCS accent (they are neumes: acute=virga, grave=punctum, 'circumflex'=clivis); dozens of OCS forms cited with the MS signs, none treated as tone marks.
sources.venue: Slovo: časopis Staroslavenskoga instituta u Zagrebu 4-5: 5-23

tone.quote: Nicht nur die Mehrzahl der akzentuierten Silben ist unbezeichnet geblieben, sondern die »Akzente« stehen auch noch sehr oft auf nichtakzentuierten Silben, ja sogar auch verschiedentlich gleichzeitig auf mehreren Silben ein und desselben Wortes. ... Man muss also an ihrer Akzentgeltung ernste Zweifel haben. ... Im ganzen kann man also sagen, entsprechen die Merkmale der Zeichen in den Ki. Bl. ... gerade den Gepflogenheiten der lateinischen Neumen für die lectio solemnis der Sakramentarien.
tone.locator: p. 11, section 2 'Die bisherigen Ansichten über Zweck und Verwendung der Zeichen'; last sentence from p. 19
tone.translation: Not only has the majority of accented syllables remained unmarked, but the 'accents' also very often stand on unaccented syllables, indeed sometimes simultaneously on several syllables of one and the same word. ... One must therefore have serious doubts about their value as accents. ... On the whole one can say that the characteristics of the signs in the Kiev Folia ... correspond precisely to the usage of the Latin neumes for the lectio solemnis of the sacramentaries.
tone.summary: Denies that the Kiev Folia diacritics record OCS accent (they are neumes: acute=virga, grave=punctum, 'circumflex'=clivis); dozens of OCS forms cited with the MS signs, none treated as tone marks.
tone.says: Denies that the Kiev Folia diacritics record OCS accent (they are neumes: acute=virga, grave=punctum, 'circumflex'=clivis); dozens of OCS forms cited with the MS signs, none treated as tone marks.

sources.citation: Koschmieder, Erwin. 1940. Die ekphonetische Notation in kirchenslawischen Sprachdenkmälern. Südost-Forschungen 5: 22-32. Leipzig.
sources.note: Palaeographic-musicological article: takes the Kiev Folia signs as prosodic plus ekphonetic (recitation) notation, not as evidence for the language's accent; no tone system stated.

tone.quote: Es besteht natürlich die Möglichkeit, daß zwei von diesen Systemen nebeneinander über einem Texte auftreten, etwa das prosodische und das ekphonetische, wie das in griechischen Handschriften vorkommt ... Einen solchen Fall habe ich in den ältesten kirchenslawischen Handschriften noch nicht mit Bestimmtheit nachgewiesen. Aber ich muß hier betonen, daß hierher eben die Kiever Blätter aller Wahrscheinlichkeit nach gehören. ... Direkt nämlich mit den griechischen ekphonetischen Zeichen lassen sich die der Kiever Blätter nur schwer in Verbindung bringen.
tone.translation: There is of course the possibility that two of these systems occur side by side over one text, e.g. the prosodic and the ekphonetic, as happens in Greek manuscripts ... I have not yet demonstrated such a case with certainty in the oldest Church Slavonic manuscripts. But I must stress here that in all probability the Kiev Folia belong precisely here. ... For the signs of the Kiev Folia can only with difficulty be connected directly with the Greek ekphonetic signs.
tone.summary: Palaeographic-musicological article: takes the Kiev Folia signs as prosodic plus ekphonetic (recitation) notation, not as evidence for the language's accent; no tone system stated.
tone.says: Palaeographic-musicological article: takes the Kiev Folia signs as prosodic plus ekphonetic (recitation) notation, not as evidence for the language's accent; no tone system stated.

sources.citation: Karinskij, N. M. 1901. Ob udarenijax v Kievskix glagoličeskix otryvkax [On the accents in the Kiev glagolitic fragments]. Izvestija Otdelenija russkogo jazyka i slovesnosti Imperatorskoj Akademii nauk 6(3): 281-289.
sources.note: Philological note on manuscript accent marks: signs mark stress by living pronunciation; acute/grave/circumflex choice is orthographic (Greek-modelled), not phonetic. No tone-labelled forms.
sources.venue: Izvestija Otdelenija russkogo jazyka i slovesnosti Imperatorskoj Akademii nauk

tone.quote: Имѣя въ виду все сказанное, мы гадательно вправѣ предположить, что 1) знаки ´, `, ^ означаютъ ударенія и заимствованы изъ греческой письменности; 2) постановка того или другого знака (остраго, тяжелаго или облеченнаго) не зависѣла отъ оттѣнковъ въ произношеніи буквы, надъ которой онъ ставился. Писцы, разставляя знаки, руководились опредѣленными правилами орѳографіи, которая отчасти стояла въ связи съ греческой; 3) ударенія, повидимому, разставлены въ то время, когда на концѣ произносился ударяемый ъ ...
tone.translation: Bearing in mind all that has been said, we may conjecturally suppose that 1) the signs ´, `, ^ denote accents and are borrowed from Greek writing; 2) the placing of one or another sign (acute, grave or circumflex) did not depend on shades in the pronunciation of the letter over which it was placed. The scribes, in placing the signs, were guided by definite rules of orthography, which in part stood in connection with the Greek; 3) the accents, apparently, were placed at a time when a stressed final ъ was still pronounced ...
tone.summary: Philological note on manuscript accent marks: signs mark stress by living pronunciation; acute/grave/circumflex choice is orthographic (Greek-modelled), not phonetic. No tone-labelled forms.
tone.says: Philological note on manuscript accent marks: signs mark stress by living pronunciation; acute/grave/circumflex choice is orthographic (Greek-modelled), not phonetic. No tone-labelled forms.
